chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Dawood ibn al-Husayn, from Umar ibn Hanzalah, who said:

I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about two men from our companions between whom there was a dispute concerning a debt or an inheritance, so they sought judgment from the ruler and from the judges. Is that permissible?

He عليه السلام said: Whoever seeks judgment from them in a matter of right or falsehood has only sought judgment from the tyrannical authority, and whatever is judged for him, he only takes as illicit gain, even if it is an established right, because he took it by the judgment of the tyrannical authority, while Allah has commanded that it be disbelieved in.
Allah, the Exalted, said: “They desire to seek judgment from the tyrannical authority, though they were commanded to disbelieve in it.”

I said: So what should the two of them do? He عليه السلام said: They should look to one among you who has narrated our hadith, examined our halal and our haram, and recognized our rulings; then let them be satisfied with him as an arbiter, for I have appointed him as a ruler over you. So if he judges by our judgment and it is not accepted from him, then the judgment of Allah has been taken lightly, and us has been rejected; and the one who rejects us rejects Allah, and he is on the verge of shirk with Allah.

I said: Then if each man chose one man from our companions, and they were both satisfied that the two should examine their right, but they differed in what they judged, and both differed regarding your hadith? He عليه السلام said: The ruling is what is judged by the one who is more just, more learned in fiqh, more truthful in hadith, and more scrupulous; and no attention is to be given to what the other rules.

He said: I said: If both of them are just and approved by our companions, and neither of them is preferred over the other? He عليه السلام said: Then one should look at what in their narrations from us concerning that matter is agreed upon by your companions; then it is to be taken from our ruling, and the anomalous report that is not well known among your companions is to be left, for that which is agreed upon has no doubt in it.

Matters are only of three kinds: a matter whose right guidance is clear, so it is followed; a matter whose error is clear, so it is avoided; and a difficult matter whose knowledge is referred back to Allah and to His Messenger. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: The halal is clear, and the haram is clear, and doubtful matters lie between them. So whoever leaves the doubtful matters is saved from the prohibited matters, and whoever takes up the doubtful matters commits the prohibited matters and perishes from where he does not know.

I said: Then if the two reports from you are both well known, and trustworthy narrators have reported them from you? He عليه السلام said: It should be considered: whatever ruling accords with the ruling of the Book and the sunnah and differs from the generality is to be taken, and what opposes the ruling of the Book and the sunnah and agrees with the generality is to be left.

I said: May I be your ransom, what if the two jurists both knew its ruling from the Book and the sunnah, and we found one of the two reports agreeing with the generality and the other opposing them; with which of the two reports is it to be taken? He عليه السلام said: That which opposes the generality, for in it is right guidance.

So I said: May I be your ransom, then if both reports agree with them altogether? He عليه السلام said: Then one should look at what their rulers and their judges are more inclined toward; that is to be left, and the other is to be taken.

I said: Then if their rulers agree with both reports altogether? He عليه السلام said: If that is so, then defer it until you meet your Imam, for pausing at doubtful matters is better than rushing into destruction.

key_terms.أَحْكَامَنَا: the legal rulings and judgments of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.الشَّاذُّ: the anomalous or isolated report that is not widely known
key_terms.الشُّبُهَاتِ: doubtful matters that are unclear between halal and haram
key_terms.الطَّاغُوتِ: the illegitimate tyrannical authority to whom judgment is wrongly referred
key_terms.الْمُجْمَعُ عَلَيْهِ: that which is agreed upon among the companions
key_terms.حَرَامِنَا: the forbidden matters as taught by the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.حَلَالِنَا: the lawful matters as taught by the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.سُحْتًا: illicitly consumed gain taken through invalid judgment

ai.seo_question: How should conflicting hadith be evaluated and legal disputes judged according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out the principles for seeking judgment in disputes and for preferring one report over another when narrations conflict. It directs the believers to qualified transmitters and jurists from among the companions of the Imams عليهم السلام, and it outlines methods of tarjih such as justice, fiqh, agreement with the Book and the sunnah, and opposition to the generality when necessary.
